paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, baker. Nebuzaradan, a Babylonian captain, says the LORD has fulfilled what He said, and that the people sinned and did not obey His voice (Jeremiah 40:2-3). God's word came true, every bit of it. So when the LORD says something, you can bake your whole day around it.

Now look at what Jeremiah does with the open door. The chains come off, the whole land is before him, and he is offered Babylon with somebody to take care of him (Jeremiah 40:4). He goes to Gedaliah and stays with the people who were left (Jeremiah 40:6). I think that says something about where his heart was. He stuck with the people God's word had been about, even when they were the poorest of the land.

Then comes the part that makes me hold my mustache. Gedaliah is warned that Ishmael wants to take his life, and he doesn't believe it (Jeremiah 40:14). He tells Johanan, "What you are saying about Ishmael is a lie." (Jeremiah 40:16). A good start, a harvest coming in and people coming home can still leave you too comfortable to listen. So stay humble, baker, and take a warning seriously, even when everything looks sweet. This story isn't over, so keep that oven warm.
